title: st.color_picker cannot be fully interacted with when it's directly inside st.dialog
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using `st.color_picker` the component does not work when it's inside `st.dialog`.  Clicking on the coloured square opens the color pallete, but any interaction with that pallete is imposible.

Putting the element inside a popover fixes the issue. I have tested `st.column`, `st.expander` and neither of them fix the issue like `st.dialog`.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

[USER].dialog("Example dialog")
def example_dialog():
    color = st.color_picker("Color picker inside dialog")
    st.text(color)

    with st.popover("Example popover"):
        color = st.color_picker("Color picker inside dialog inside popover")
        st.text(color)


color = st.color_picker("Color picker inside dialog inside popover")
st.text(color)

st.button("Click me", on_click=example_dialog)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create `st.dialog`
2. Create `st.color_picker` inside that dialog
3. Try to interact with the `st.color_picker`

### Expected Behavior

The color pallete would be interactable with inside st.dialog.

### Current Behavior

Upon clicking on `st.color_picker` that is inside `st.dialog` the color pallete dropdown opens, but user cannot interact with it with mouse nor keyboard.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: Python 3.12.4
- Operating System: Windows 11 (OS build 26100.9106)
- I have tested this behaviour on following browsers and the unexpected behaviour was same for all
    - Microsoft Edge (Version 151.0.4129.78) (Official build) (64-bit)
    - Firefox Version 153.0.4 (64-bit)
    - Google Chrome (Version 151.0.7922.138) (Official Build) (64-bit)


### Additional Information

_No response_

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16538)

This is a frontend bug: `st.color_picker` opens its palette inside `st.dialog`, but mouse and keyboard interaction with the palette fail. Likely root cause: `BaseColorPicker` mounts via `<FloatingPortal>` without `id={FLOATING_OVERLAY_PORTAL_ID}`, so the popover is not under the shared host tagged with `data-react-aria-top-layer` / `data-st-overlay-root`. React Aria’s dialog then treats that portal as outside the modal (often marking it `inert`), which matches “opens but cannot interact.” Nesting under `st.popover` can appear to work because popover already uses that portal host. The same fix pattern used for date_input / selectbox / popover-in-dialog overlays should apply here.

### Related Issues

- [#16005](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16005) — Popover content inside a dialog was unusable for the same React Aria overlay/`inert` reason; fixed by routing Floating UI portals through `FLOATING_OVERLAY_PORTAL_ID`. Closest prior art for this bug.
- [#15859](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15859) — `st.date_input` calendar rendered behind / unusable inside `st.dialog` (overlay stacking after the React Aria dialog migration). Same dialog + portaled overlay family.
- [#15599](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15599) — Selectbox dropdown behind `st.dialog` so clicks did not register. Same class of dialog overlay interaction issues.

No exact open duplicate found for `st.color_picker` specifically.
